results.label: Blanc
notes: main.js creates one blanc://newtab at startup in addition to the URLs
passed on the command line — hence extraBlankTabs: 1.
Blanc CANCELS every http(s) main-frame request until its blocker is
compiled (installStartupNavigationGate, main.js:226/3751). On a cold
profile that gate can stay shut for the whole sampling window, so the
runner warms a template profile first and verifies every loaded cell
against the browser's own idle baseline.
Do NOT set BLANC_TEST=1 for a benchmark run: acceptanceTestMode in
main.js disables ad blocking, which would measure a configuration the
app never ships.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

results.label: Blanc (blocking off)
notes: Isolates what the built-in blocker contributes. The runner seeds
settings.json in the throwaway profile with adblockEnabled: false.
Shares a bundle path with the 'blanc' entry, so a process surviving one
cell would be attributed to the other — which is why quit() reaps the
whole measured process set rather than just the root pid.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

results.label: Google Chrome
notes: The report's reference row: percentages are relative to Chrome rather
than to whichever browser scored lowest.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

results.label: Brave
notes: Brave's updater (Sparkle) lives inside the app bundle and keeps its
check state in ~/Library/Preferences, which --user-data-dir does not
reset — so a fresh profile does not prevent an update check firing mid
measurement. --disable-brave-update suppresses it. This changes no
process-model knob, so it does not violate the no-flags rule; the Gecko
driver already sets app.update.auto=false for the same reason.
UNVERIFIED: whether Brave opens a welcome tab on a fresh profile despite
--no-first-run. If it does, extraBlankTabs must be raised.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

results.label: Vivaldi
results.blocking: built-in blocker, trackers only at stock settings
notes: Vivaldi ships its blocker set to block trackers, NOT ads, out of the
box; the registry previously said 'built-in blocker (stock settings)',
which read as an ad-blocking peer and would have grouped it with Blanc
and Brave. UNVERIFIED against a real install — confirm in Settings >
Privacy before publishing, since a wrong class silently moves the row
into the wrong comparison group.
Vivaldi's own UI is a web page rendered in a renderer process, so its
process count and baseline include the browser chrome itself — the same
property Blanc has, and unlike Chrome's native UI.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.

results.label: Zen Browser
results.blocking: ETP Standard — tracker cookies, cryptominers, fingerprinters; does NOT block ads, and blocks tracking content only in private windows
notes: Zen ships its own onboarding, separate from Mozilla's about:welcome, so
browser.aboutwelcome.enabled=false does not touch it. Every cell mints a
fresh profile, so every Zen cell is a first run; its welcome flow hides
the browser content until a human clicks through, which would settle
fast and clean and be recorded as an excellent result at the requested
tab count. extraPrefs sets the pref that suppresses it — if a future
build renames it, the welcome screen returns silently and only the load
check against Zen's own idle baseline catches it.
CONFIRMED 2026-08-09 on Zen 1.x / macOS 27: user.js startup-homepage
tab seeding IS honoured — the upstream report of it failing on macOS
aarch64 (zen-browser/desktop#12154) did not reproduce here. But Zen
consumes the FIRST startup entry with its own workspace/new-tab
surface, so the first workload URL was silently dropped (9/10 pages,
twice, deterministically). geckoUserJs now leads with about:blank to
absorb that.
results.workloadDescription: Startup cost only. Subtracted from loaded runs to get per-tab marginal cost.
